source_review.notes: Checked all fourteen references. Current account factory, enrollment, organization, account-structure, subscription-vending, product-line, project hierarchy, landing-zone, and foundation deployment guidance was verified against official AWS, Microsoft, and Google Cloud documentation. Platform framing and cloud access-control guidance were checked against CNCF and NIST sources. Provider-specific claims are retrieval-dated and qualified; durable vending principles are presented provider-neutrally.

evidence: Reviewed request tuple V; workload/environment/product/container/baseline/group/allocation sets; create and mapping functions; readiness predicate set; independent inventory coverage; and scarce-capacity inequality.
Confirmed tuple, set, function, cardinality, fraction, inequality, and subscript notation is defined and GitHub-renderable.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates request identity, provider identity, readiness evidence, inventory scope, and allocation capacity.

evidence: Executed the vending-state audit and reproduced active=4 and one each creating, verifying, suspended, closing, failed, and ambiguous, totaling ten records.
Checked C_i=M/N boundary assumptions N>0 and M in [0,N], giving a ratio in [0,1] without claiming mapping accuracy.
Checked allocation inequality R+A+x+S<=K and the boundary where equality consumes all capacity while preserving the declared safety reserve.
numerical_recomputation.notes: State counts and capacity arithmetic illustrate mechanisms; provider reconciliation and authority evidence remain required.

evidence: Verified stable request occurrence plus provider idempotency/reconciliation is required for repeated create attempts to converge on one provider ID.
Verified readiness is conjunction over blocking predicates and cannot be inferred from orchestration or configuration-submission success alone.
Verified catalog-only denominators omit missing provider containers and therefore cannot establish independent inventory coverage.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter does not claim one account-to-environment mapping or one readiness set is universally correct.

evidence: Reviewed duplicate/retried starts, commit-before-timeout, provider eventual consistency, partial baseline, quota denial, policy lag, bootstrap residue, address/name collision, and allocation restore.

Reviewed shared versus dedicated environments, regulated data, unmanaged adoption, owner departure/transfer, hierarchy relocation, product upgrades, provider limit exhaustion, and cross-tenant access.
Reviewed compromise suspension, expiration, unknown data, legal hold, delayed bills, closing waits, recycling, catalog/ingestion absence, provider ambiguity, and disaster recovery.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans creation, identity, hierarchy, baseline, capacity, handoff, drift, organizational change, closure, and recovery.

evidence: Traced one occurrence/one container, immutable provider identity, bounded offering, authority resolution, and effective baseline through request, create, discover, place, and verify sections.
Traced privilege separation, allocation safety, lifecycle honesty, provider truth, and transfer continuity through identity, IPAM, workflow, reconciliation, and transfer examples.
Traced deletion restraint and recoverable evidence through expiration, suspension, closure, provider waiting periods, backup, and restore.
invariant_checking.notes: Vending owns intent and lifecycle coordination while the provider remains authoritative for container existence.

evidence: Reviewed two indistinguishable catalog views: intentional retirement versus ingestion/authorization failure with a live production container.
Confirmed an absence-triggered deletion rule acts identically and therefore deletes unsafely in the second world.
Confirmed the conclusion is limited to insufficiency of catalog absence and names provider identity plus approved disposition as necessary additional evidence.
proof_review.notes: The proof does not claim the presented closure checklist is sufficient for every organization or provider.

evidence: The catalog-absence argument is explicitly labeled a proof sketch.
Its indistinguishable worlds, unsafe inference, conclusion, and checklist limitation are stated.
Container-boundary heuristics, product lines, readiness checks, and provider guidance remain policy- or evidence-bounded.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No one-container-per-environment heuristic is presented as a theorem.

evidence: The executable audit is explicitly synthetic and disclaims provider creation, baseline enforcement, and lifecycle assurance.
Current cloud guidance is attributed and retrieval-dated; worked cases remain pedagogical rather than production reports.

Required production evidence includes provider inventories/receipts, effective-policy reads, identity positive/negative tests, audit delivery probes, allocation transactions, drift checks, closure disposition, and restore reconciliation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No achieved lead time, baseline conformance, provider capacity, external review, or safe closure is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed boundary semantics, environment mapping, product lines, request/authorization, durable state, create/enroll/adopt, hierarchy, identity, baselines, connectivity contract, quota, cost, readiness, reconciliation, upgrades, transfer, suspension/closure, metrics, and recovery.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementability with stable request/provider identities, operation receipts, transactional allocation, allowed hierarchy selection, idempotent baselines, effective-state probes, scoped bootstrap workers, responsibility handoff, provider reconciliation, and evidence-driven closure.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified required section order, dense one-page review, defined notation, twelve-part protocol, fifteen trade-offs, twenty-five misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, ten cross-program connections, fourteen references, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
